newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amcoal looks forward to rise in 97/98 EPS.
newsitem.headline: Amcoal looks forward to rise in 97/98 EPS.

text.p: South Africa's Anglo American Coal Corp Ltd, one of the world's biggest coal producers, is expected to show a marginal improvement in earnings for the current year ending March 31, 1998, the South African group said on Friday.
Chairman David Rankin said in his annual review that although export tonnage were seen rising in the year, prices in U.S. dollars are forecast to be slightly lower.
"Assuming a relatively unchanged rand/U.S. dollar exchange rate, some reduction in export earnings can thus be anticipated," Rankin said.
Increased tonnages were anticipated from collieries supplying electricity utility Eskom and the inland market.

He said that Amcoal's Verref division, which produces refractories and building products including clay pipes and tiles, was forecast to show better earnings due to improving market conditions, increased efficiencies and the introduction of new products.
"With this operational background and with interest income expected to be higher, it is anticiapted that Amcoal's earnings for the year ahead will show a marginal improvement," Rankin said.
In the year to March 31, 1997 Amcoal's earnings rose 30 percent to 3,459.8 cents a share. It declared a dividend of 1,320.0 cents per unit.
